Playbook.name: Windows — Registry Persistence: IFEO / Winlogon / AppInit - SOC Playbook

Technique.name: Event Triggered Execution: Image File Execution Options Injection
Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Winlogon Helper DLL

Reference.title: MITRE ATT and CK T1546.012 Image File Execution Options Injection
MITRE ATT and CK T1547.004 Winlogon Helper DLL
MITRE ATT and CK T1546.010 AppInit DLLs

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: A Sysmon registry-value-set event (event 13) modified one of three classic autostart persistence locations: an Image File Execution Options Debugger/GlobalFlag entry, the AppInit_DLLs value, or a Winlogon Shell/Userinit/Notify value. Each of these causes attacker code to run automatically - when a target program launches (IFEO), when any process loads user32.dll (AppInit), or at every interactive logon (Winlogon). The triage question is whether a legitimate installer/patch made the change, or an attacker planted an autostart hook.
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: These hijacks give an attacker durable, high-privilege execution that survives reboots and password resets. An IFEO Debugger on an accessibility binary (sethc.exe, utilman.exe) yields SYSTEM at the logon screen; a Winlogon Userinit/Shell change or AppInit DLL runs attacker code in every session on the host - on a banking server that is a persistent backdoor into core operations.

Assets.AssetType: Windows workstations and servers running Sysmon (INTDOM)
Privileged/administrative endpoints and jump hosts (highest impact)

LogSources.LogSource: Sysmon registry events - logs-windows.sysmon_operational-* (event.code 13 value set, 12 key create)

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Sysmon registry auditing shipped to logs-windows.sysmon_operational-* with event.code 13 present (verified live: ~31k code-13 events in 7 days) and IFEO/Winlogon/Run writes observed.
registry.path, registry.value, registry.data.strings and process.executable populated keyword fields (verified live).

Signal.Name: IFEO injection
Signal.Details: registry.path under Image File Execution Options with value Debugger or GlobalFlag - Debugger redirects a target exe to an attacker binary.

Signal.Name: AppInit DLLs
Signal.Details: registry.value AppInit_DLLs set to a DLL path that loads into every user32-linked process.

Signal.Name: Winlogon hijack
Signal.Details: registry.path under Winlogon with value Shell, Userinit or Notify changed to include attacker code that runs at logon.

Input.name: $host
Input.description: Host where the registry persistence value was written (host.name from the alert).

Input.name: $user
Input.description: User context of the writing process (user.name from the alert).

Input.name: $process
Input.description: Full path of the process that wrote the value (process.executable from the alert).

ImmediateCapture.Item: Which family fired (IFEO Debugger/GlobalFlag, AppInit_DLLs, or Winlogon Shell/Userinit/Notify) and the registry.data.strings payload
For IFEO: the target executable named in the registry path (e.g. sethc.exe, an EDR/AV binary)

InitialAssessment.Rule: If $process is a trusted installer/patch component (msiexec, TrustedInstaller, a signed vendor updater) and the data points to a legitimate signed binary/DLL, lean False Positive / Misconfiguration - but read the payload before concluding.
If the payload points to a script host, a temp/user-writable path, or an unsigned binary, or the IFEO target is an accessibility or security binary, escalate as a persistence backdoor.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the registry autostart change on $host is a legitimate install/patch or attacker persistence, identify the payload it points to, and scope how far it spread.

Step.name: Read the persistence write and its payload
Step.Purpose: Surface exactly what was set - the path, value, payload data and writing process - so the analyst can judge the target and the code it points to.
Step.Query: FROM logs-windows.sysmon_operational-* | WHERE @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours AND host.name == "$host" AND event.code == "13" AND ( (TO_LOWER(registry.path) LIKE "*image file execution options*" AND registry.value IN ("Debugger","GlobalFlag")) OR registry.value == "AppInit_DLLs" OR (TO_LOWER(registry.path) LIKE "*winlogon*" AND registry.value IN ("Shell","Userinit","Notify")) ) | STATS writes=COUNT(*), first_seen=MIN(@timestamp), last_seen=MAX(@timestamp), values=VALUES(registry.value), data=VALUES(registry.data.strings), procs=VALUES(process.executable) BY registry.path, user.name | SORT writes DESC | LIMIT 100
Step.AnalystNotes: Read data (registry.data.strings) carefully. Winlogon Userinit should be exactly C:\Windows\system32\userinit.exe, and Shell should be explorer.exe - anything appended is malicious. An IFEO Debugger pointing at cmd.exe/powershell/a temp path is a backdoor. AppInit_DLLs pointing to a non-vendor DLL is persistence.

Step.name: Profile the writing process
Step.Purpose: Establish what wrote the value and where it came from. A signed installer is very different from a script host or an unsigned binary in a user-writable path.
Step.Query: FROM logs-windows.sysmon_operational-* | WHERE @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours AND host.name == "$host" AND event.code == "1" AND process.executable == "$process" | STATS starts=COUNT(*), first_seen=MIN(@timestamp), cmds=VALUES(process.command_line), parents=VALUES(process.parent.executable), parent_names=VALUES(process.parent.name) BY process.name, user.name | SORT starts DESC | LIMIT 50
Step.AnalystNotes: msiexec.exe / TrustedInstaller.exe / a signed vendor updater under services.exe is consistent with a legitimate install. reg.exe/powershell.exe/wscript.exe writing these keys, or a process launched by an Office app or from a temp path, indicates hands-on persistence.

Step.name: Map the persistence landscape on the host
Step.Purpose: Determine whether this write is isolated or one of several autostart changes planted together (attackers commonly stack persistence).
Step.Query: FROM logs-windows.sysmon_operational-* | WHERE @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours AND host.name == "$host" AND event.code IN ("12","13") AND ( TO_LOWER(registry.path) LIKE "*image file execution options*" OR TO_LOWER(registry.path) LIKE "*winlogon*" OR TO_LOWER(registry.path) LIKE "*appinit*" OR TO_LOWER(registry.path) LIKE "*currentversion*run*" ) | STATS writes=COUNT(*), values=VALUES(registry.value), procs=VALUES(process.executable) BY registry.path | SORT writes DESC | LIMIT 100
Step.AnalystNotes: Multiple autostart changes (IFEO plus a Run key plus a Winlogon edit) in the same window by the same process is a strong persistence-cluster signal. A single change from a known updater is more consistent with a patch.

Step.name: Scope how far the writing process spread the change
Step.Purpose: Determine whether $process wrote the same persistence on many hosts (mass deployment - attacker tooling or an unexpected GPO) versus a single targeted host.
Step.Query: FROM logs-windows.sysmon_operational-* | WHERE @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours AND event.code == "13" AND process.executable == "$process" AND ( (TO_LOWER(registry.path) LIKE "*image file execution options*" AND registry.value IN ("Debugger","GlobalFlag")) OR registry.value == "AppInit_DLLs" OR (TO_LOWER(registry.path) LIKE "*winlogon*" AND registry.value IN ("Shell","Userinit","Notify")) ) | STATS writes=COUNT(*), hosts=COUNT_DISTINCT(host.name), host_list=VALUES(host.name), values=VALUES(registry.value) BY process.executable | LIMIT 20
Step.AnalystNotes: Writes across many hosts by the same executable point to either a sanctioned management/GPO deployment (verify with the platform team) or a spreading attacker. A single host with an anomalous writing process is targeted persistence.

Node.Condition: INV-01 payload points to a script host, user-writable/temp path, or unsigned binary, OR the IFEO target is an accessibility/security binary, OR Winlogon Userinit/Shell has content appended beyond the OS defaults - and INV-02 shows an untrusted writing process.
Node.Result: True Positive (autostart persistence backdoor - escalate to IR immediately)

Node.Condition: INV-04 shows the same change written across many hosts by a process that cannot be confirmed as a sanctioned management/GPO deployment.
Node.Result: Needs Escalation (possible mass persistence - confirm deployment source urgently)

Node.Condition: INV-02 shows a trusted installer/patch component (msiexec, TrustedInstaller, signed vendor updater) wrote the value and INV-01 data points to a legitimate signed binary/DLL consistent with that software.
A known management tool or driver package legitimately sets IFEO GlobalFlag/AppInit on a schedule (e.g. an EDR/AV or debugging config) and trips the rule as recurring noise.
Node.Result: Misconfiguration (tune for the specific tool/value; do not broadly exception the persistence paths)

Node.Condition: Writing process or payload cannot be attributed, or signals are mixed.

FalsePositive.Definition: A legitimate installer, patch or management tool wrote the value - an authorised and attributable software action, not merely an assumed-benign change.

Indicators.Item: Writing process is a signed installer/updater or TrustedInstaller under a normal service parent (INV-02).
Payload data is a legitimate signed binary/DLL in a system path consistent with the software.
Change coincides with a known deployment/patch window.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm the install/patch with the platform or endpoint team.
If a specific management tool is chronically noisy, propose a scoped tuning for that value/process only.
Close as false_positive with the change reference attached.

TruePositive.Definition: An attacker planted a registry autostart hook for durable, privileged execution.

Indicators.Item: IFEO Debugger redirecting a target (especially sethc.exe/utilman.exe or a security binary) to attacker code.
Winlogon Userinit/Shell/Notify or AppInit_DLLs pointing to a script host, temp/user path, or unsigned DLL (INV-01).
Untrusted writing process (reg.exe/powershell/wscript or an Office-spawned process) and/or a persistence cluster (INV-03).

SOCAction.Item: Isolate $host; capture the payload binary/DLL and the registry value before remediation.
Remove the malicious value/restore the OS default (e.g. reset Userinit/Shell), and hunt for the payload executing.
Open an incident; determine initial access via the writing process lineage (INV-02) and check other hosts (INV-04).

Misconfiguration.Definition: A legitimate tool or configuration writes these keys by design (e.g. an EDR setting GlobalFlag, a debugging IFEO entry) and generates recurring alerts.

Indicators.Item: Same benign value/process recurring on a schedule with a signed, expected payload.
No untrusted writer, no cluster of unrelated persistence changes.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm the tool/configuration with its owner.
Tune the rule for the specific value/process; track under detection-tuning, not IR.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: If the payload is untrusted (INV-01), isolate $host and preserve the registry value and the referenced binary/DLL.
Identify the writing process lineage (INV-02) and check for the same change on other hosts (INV-04).

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Remove the malicious value and restore OS defaults (Userinit/Shell), delete attacker DLL/binary, kill any running payload.
Determine and remediate initial access; reset credentials used on the host if compromise is confirmed.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Reimage if SYSTEM-level persistence is confirmed; validate Winlogon/AppInit/IFEO values across the affected tier.
Consider AppInit_DLLs disablement policy and monitoring of accessibility-binary IFEO entries.

Escalation.Trigger: Any untrusted payload in an autostart value, an IFEO Debugger on an accessibility/security binary, a persistence cluster, or the same change across multiple hosts without a confirmed deployment source.

FalsePositiveClosure.Item: Install/patch/management change verified with the owning team and matches the process and payload.
Payload confirmed as a legitimate signed binary/DLL; no cluster of unrelated persistence changes.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Malicious value removed/defaults restored, payload eradicated, host isolated or reimaged.
Initial access identified, spread scoped across hosts, and follow-on execution ruled out.
